correctness.rationale: After the first two outgoing edges, the subsequent globally uniform shuffle places two unit piles at a uniform unordered pair S of distinct vertices; no unjustified independent-ball approximation is made. Empty indicator at target v is 1[S cap N(v)=empty], giving E Z2=d*C(d-2,2)/H=mu. For a,b, k_ab=|N(a) cap N(b)| and P(both empty)=C(d-4+k_ab,2)/H. The global codegree sum over a<b is d, while k_ab=2 exactly at the two opposite pairs per C4 component, so E C(Z2,2)=(H*C(d-4,2)+d(d-4)+2q)/H. This gives variance. A fresh independent global permutation sends the two input neighbors of any target to a uniform pair, so E[Z3/d]=E C(Z2,2)/H. Simple-cycle partitions classify extremal q and first q-variation at d=7. Direct exact enumeration of all cycle partitions d=7..14 and uniform pairs corroborated 156 formulas; unrestricted conclusion follows from the codegree counting.

value.rationale: PASS: a sharp first graph-geometric signature at finite depth in an otherwise geometry-independent asymptotic occupancy model is a motivated structural counterpoint. The 4-cycle motif coefficient and all cycle-partition extremizers yield a complete natural subclass classification, including the smallest witness size d=7. Its small asymptotic magnitude is disclosed but does not remove mathematical interest.

final_claim: For any simple undirected 2-regular graph on d>=7 vertices with independently uniformly shuffled full pile vectors between path-expansion layers, E[Z2]=mu, Var(Z2)=2(A+2q)/H+mu-mu^2, and E[Z3/d]=(A+2q)/H^2, with q the C4-component count and explicit q-extremizers and sharp d=7 onset.
limitations: No full law of Z3, no higher-layer or higher-regularity classification; the C4 effect becomes asymptotically small in some regimes.
